# ReClip

> ReClip is an MIT-licensed, open-source interface for inspecting and downloading media with yt-dlp. It supports full downloads and precise clips with optional millisecond timestamps.

Use ReClip when a user wants to save permitted video or audio, extract audio, select video quality, process multiple links, or download only a time range. Users must have the right to download the requested media and must comply with the source platform's terms.

## Public Web App

- [Open ReClip](https://daddy23-reclip.hf.space/): Hosted browser interface
- The hosted service supports many yt-dlp sites, but YouTube currently rejects requests from its datacenter IP. Use the local app for YouTube.
- Do not invoke `/api/` endpoints through a crawler. Downloads require an explicit user action.
- [Hosted API reference](https://daddy23-reclip.hf.space/api-docs): OpenAPI documentation for the resource-limited interactive service
- [OpenAPI document](https://daddy23-reclip.hf.space/openapi.json): Machine-readable API contract

## Local App

- [Source and installation](https://github.com/yagyaanshK/reclip): Runs on the user's computer and network
- [Latest releases](https://github.com/yagyaanshK/reclip/releases/latest): Desktop downloads when release artifacts are available

## Capabilities

- Inspect a media URL before download
- Download video with a selected available resolution
- Extract audio as MP3
- Download a clip using `SS`, `MM:SS`, or `HH:MM:SS.000` start/end values
- Process multiple URLs while retaining per-item format and clip controls

## Limitations

- Site support changes as source websites change; current behavior is determined by the installed yt-dlp version.
- Login-protected, DRM-protected, private, paid, or otherwise restricted media may not work and must not be bypassed.
- The public instance is resource-limited and is not a general-purpose automation API.
